headline: Fed holds steady today while Big Tech earnings test AI spending
body: Markets are parked on Fed decision day. The FOMC is due to announce its rate call this afternoon, and previews cite prediction-market and rate-futures pricing putting the odds of a hold at the current 3.75%-4.00% range near 90%. That near-certainty sits awkwardly next to the data behind it: September inflation accelerated to roughly 3.7% year-over-year even as nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, a combination pulling policymakers in opposite directions. Economist surveys lean almost unanimous that today's hold is a pause rather than a pivot, with consensus pointing to another hike in December rather than a cut; prediction-market traders are a bit less convinced, pricing that December move closer to 75%. With the headline decision this well telegraphed, the more market-moving moment is likely Chair Warsh's press conference commentary on the inflation-growth tradeoff, not the vote itself.

The Fed news lands in the middle of Big Tech's earnings week, with Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet reporting and Amazon to follow, all under scrutiny for AI capital-spending plans after that narrative has been the market's main swing factor recently. Major indices pulled back from fresh record highs earlier this month, with one recent session showing the Nasdaq Composite down over 2% on tech and communication-services weakness before a partial recovery -- a market that looks less confidently bullish than the record-high headlines from early October suggested. Retail-sentiment chatter on forums like WallStreetBets didn't surface a clear, current read in today's search, so this take leans more on the earnings-and-Fed news flow and recent price action than on observed social-media positioning.
